meta.title: Lump Sum Beat Dollar-Cost Averaging About Two-Thirds Of The Time
meta.hook: Vanguard found investing a lump sum immediately won roughly two-thirds of historical periods.
meta.description: Vanguard research found immediate lump-sum investing historically outperformed staged cost averaging roughly two-thirds of the time because more money spent more time invested. Cost averaging can reduce short-term timing risk and regret. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Vanguard found investing a lump sum immediately beat staged cost averaging in roughly two-thirds of historical periods.

visual.visual_intent: Cash splitting into immediate and scheduled investment paths
visual.decision_reason: Vanguard research reports the roughly two-thirds historical result

scenes.narration: The reason is simple: markets have generally risen over time, so cash waiting on the sidelines has an opportunity cost.

visual.query: stock market long term rising chart
visual.visual_intent: A long-term market chart with cash waiting beside it
visual.decision_reason: Vanguard attributes the result to opportunity cost and risk premium

scenes.narration: Dollar-cost averaging moves equal portions in on a schedule, reducing the risk of investing everything just before a drop.

visual.visual_intent: Equal dollar amounts entering a portfolio across calendar dates
visual.decision_reason: Vanguard defines cost averaging and its temporary risk reduction

scenes.narration: But that protection also means part of the money stays in cash longer if the market rises.

visual.visual_intent: A cash stack stationary while a chart climbs
visual.decision_reason: Direct tradeoff identified in Vanguard research

scenes.narration: So this is a tradeoff between higher expected time in the market and lower short-term timing regret.

visual.visual_intent: A scale labeled time invested and timing regret
visual.decision_reason: Balanced summary of expected return versus loss aversion

scenes.narration: Neither method removes market risk. The useful question is which plan an investor can actually follow through volatility.

visual.visual_intent: A person calmly following a written investment plan
visual.decision_reason: Avoids personalized recommendation and acknowledges market risk
